@tbl-libraries compares the particle filter benchmarks of @tbl-timing-full across Python particle filter libraries, with each model written as a user of that library would write it.

::: {#tbl-libraries}
```{python}
#| echo: false

lib_times = pd.read_csv(QUANT / "tests" / "library_comparison" / "table.csv")
lib_times = lib_times.set_index(["model", "column"])
lib_version = lib_times["version"].dropna().groupby(level="column").first()


def fmt_s(x):
    if x is None or pd.isna(x):
        return "---"
    return f"{x:,.0f}" if x >= 100 else f"{x:.1f}"


def fmt_lib(model, column):
    row = lib_times.loc[(model, column)]
    if row["status"] == "timeout":
        return f"$>${row['first_s']:,.0f}"
    return fmt_s(row["first_s"])


rows = []
for model, label in TIMING_MODELS.items():
    libs = [
        fmt_lib(model, c)
        for c in ["pypomp", "pfjax", "cuthbert", "pydpf", "particles", "pypfilt"]
    ]
    r = fmt_s(pf_time(timing[model]["R"]["times"]))
    rows.append(f"{label} & " + " & ".join(libs) + f" & {r}")
tbl = latex_table(
    "lrrrrrrr",
    [
        " & \\multicolumn{4}{c}{1 GPU} & \\multicolumn{3}{c}{36 CPU cores} \\\\",
        "\\cmidrule(lr){2-5} \\cmidrule(lr){6-8}",
        "Model & Pypomp & \\texttt{pfjax} & \\texttt{cuthbert} & \\texttt{pydpf} "
        "& \\texttt{particles}$^\\dagger$ & \\texttt{pypfilt}$^\\dagger$ & \\texttt{pomp}$^*$ \\\\",
    ],
    rows,
)
# Eight columns fit the text width only with slightly tighter column spacing.
Markdown(tbl.data.replace("\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{4pt}", "\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{3pt}"))
```

Wall-clock time in seconds for the particle filter benchmarks of @tbl-timing-full in Pypomp `{python} lib_version["pypomp"]`, `pfjax` `{python} lib_version["pfjax"]` and `cuthbert` `{python} lib_version["cuthbert"]` (JAX), `pydpf` `{python} lib_version["pydpf"]` (PyTorch), and `particles` `{python} lib_version["particles"]` and `pypfilt` `{python} lib_version["pypfilt"]` (NumPy). GPU times are from one RTX 3090, which is slower than the GPU in @tbl-timing, and include JIT compilation. For the measles models, `pfjax` and `cuthbert` draw with the `jax.random` samplers (Appendix -@sec-samplers), and neither finished the 4-town panel within an hour. $^\dagger$`particles` and `pypfilt` run only on CPUs; their times are the time for one filter on one core, multiplied by the number of filters and divided by 36, which assumes perfect scaling over 36 cores. $^*$`panelPomp` for the 4-town panel, as in @tbl-timing-full.
:::
